name: pip
title: Shoulder printed in place: its numbers, and the carrier (not printed)
description: Nothing to print: the numbers the print-in-place shoulder's parts are drawn from (shoulder-pip and the assembly's shoulder-pip-* objects read them), and a speck that carries the planets' joints in the assembly, where they ride on the sun and the two rings.

ratio.rule: Turns of the sun for one of the output: the nearest compoundPlanetary finds with the bigger planet step on the sun and the held ring, so the planets and the sun print on what is below them

step.rule: The output ring's teeth fewer than the held ring's, by the planets: the planets' lower step smaller, on the output ring

sun.rule: Teeth on the sun, as compoundPlanetary finds them

planet.rule: Teeth on the planets' upper step, on the sun and the held ring

planet2.rule: Teeth on the planets' lower step, on the output ring

ring.rule: Teeth on the held ring, in the housing

gap.rule: Between every two parts, each side: what prints apart

spare.rule: Drawn on top of the print gap, so the straight facets of drawn rounds don't eat into it: a 96-sided circle 35 mm across the middle falls 0.019 mm inside its round, and Manifold measured the gaps drawn at the bare print gap 0.292 to 0.297 mm

clear.rule: Every gap as drawn: the print gap and the facets' allowance

foot.rule: How far the first layer spreads each side as it is squashed on

layer.rule: The first layer: the teeth on the bed are cut straight, with the gap it needs, for this high

bed_addendum.rule: The teeth's height over the pitch circle on the first layer, in modules: teeth thinned to the first layer's gap come to a point at ISO 53's 1; the layers above carry the drive

chamfer.rule: Off the bed edges that face another part, against the first layer's spread

comp.rule: How much a printed hole shrinks, for the sun's bore

low.rule: The output stage's face: the assembled shoulder's

high.rule: The held stage's face, as the assembled shoulder's

rim2.rule: Round the output ring: its 59.8 mm root, the arm's pilots and two lines of wall each side of them

bolt.rule: Radius of the arm's pilots, between the output ring's root and its rim

pilot_depth.rule: The arm's pilots, as deep as the output ring's cut-back top leaves

wall.rule: The housing's skirt round the output ring: six lines

opening.rule: The roof's hole, for the sun's hub: as wide as the motor's posts leave, so the roof's cone is short

lip.rule: The roof's inner edge above its cone: five layers

plate.rule: Each post's top over its window, under the motor: one and a half of its screws' diameters, the least v.motors' mountModel takes before a head pulls through. pipScrews (shoulder-pip-parts.js) names the screw through v.fixings, the motor's own thread at the longest length sold that stays in its tapped holes, and fails the build if mountModel finds the screw short or the plate thin

hub.rule: The sun's hub up to the motor, round the 5 mm shaft

face.value: low + clear + high + clear + centre + module * (planet + 2) / 2 + clear - opening / 2 + lip + window_h + (window_w - bridge) / 2 + plate
face.rule: The motor's face, on its posts: the roof's cone rising at 45° from a gap over the planets' upper step, its lip, then the posts' windows and tops

far.rule: Under the bed, clear of every part and the motor

sixty.rule: Each planet from the x axis

straight.rule: The held stage's first six layers cut straight, not as a herringbone: where the housing's underside and the planets' upper step widen at 45° (up to 1.1 mm above the stage's foot at the held ring's tips) a twist as well leans past what prints

window_w.rule: Each post's window across: the motor's screw's hexagon head across its corners (v.fixings' screwModel, held to it by pipScrews) and an open spanner's jaws round them

window_h.rule: Each post's window, upright, before its top rises: the hexagon head's height (v.fixings' screwModel, held to it by pipScrews) and a spanner's thickness

bridge.rule: The widest flat the window's top may span

post_r.rule: Each post, along its window: the screw's hole and two lines of wall each side

post_w.rule: Each post, across its window: the window and two millimetres of wall each side

ring_turn.rule: How far the held ring is turned from the sun's frame so the planets mesh it, as compoundPlanetary lays the gearbox out (its ring.angle): the housing's axis is turned back by this, so the parts on it sit as they print
